Maya Patel: Heads-up — saw a burst of 429s for tenant=alpha when GPU pool hit memory pressure and queues backed up. Thinking we should standardize a 'rate-scarcity fallback' playbook: prefer model-size fallback -> reduce max_tokens -> fall back to cache -> return 429 w/ Retry-After as last resort.
Tomas Chen: can you paste the logs? which component emitted the 429s? :eyes:
Maya Patel: snippet from ingress-proxy:
`ingress-proxy admit failure: capacity-exhausted shard=eu-west-1b tenant=alpha tokens=134k queue_len=142 backpressure=soft`
Lisa G: +1 to a fallback chain. Question: do we prefer switching to a smaller model or accepting higher latency? For tier=standard maybe smaller model is okay; for enterprise maybe we keep same model but enqueue.
Anjali R: for dedicated customers we should never auto-downgrade without explicit consent. must be opt-in via tenant routing policy.
Maya Patel: agree — policy layers: global default, tenant override, dedicated override. propose schema for fallback config:
```json
{"fallback_order": ["defer","smaller_model","truncate_input","use_cached_prefix","reject"], "min_slo_ms": 50, "allow_downgrade_for_tier": ["free","standard"]}
```
Tomas Chen: small nit: 'defer' should be explicit 'defer_enqueue' vs 'defer_busy-wait'. Also need signals: memory_pressure vs kernel-queue-saturation; how do we decide it's safe to downgrade vs just backoff?
Lisa G: add hysteresis & cooldown. e.g., only trigger downgrade if p95_latency > target for 3s AND gpu_mem_used > 90% for 5s. prevents flapping.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: canary rollout for fallback-policy v1 started on eng-runtime-canary-2 at 4718001240 :rocket:
Maya Patel: telemetry we need: fallback_count, fallback_path, quality_impact_eval_id, tenant_override_count. tag by model_version and region.
Tomas Chen: billing impact: downgrading model changes per-token cost. ledger must record a billing_adjustment and each admission decision needs an idempotency token so retries don't double-charge.
Anjali R: also consider abuse: clients could craft requests to intentionally trigger cheaper-model fallback (huge prefix, long prompt) to save cost. Need abuse detection: track repeated fallback triggers -> deprioritize or require higher auth.
Lisa G: implementation idea: admission controller state machine: ACCEPT -> DEFER_ENQUEUE -> FALLBACK -> REJECT. transitions based on counters and short-lived state stored in Redis (cooldown token).
Maya Patel: sample pseudocode for admission logic:
```python
if tenant.has_dedicated(): return ACCEPT
if gpu_mem_pct > 90 and p95_latency > target and cooldown == 0:
    return FALLBACK(smaller_model)
if queue_len > 100 and can_use_prefix_cache(req):
    return FALLBACK(use_cached_prefix)
if fallback_attempts > 2:
    return REJECT(429, headers={"Retry-After": 10})
```
Tomas Chen: API surface: when we fallback, return structured headers so clients can react: `X-Redwood-Fallback: smaller-model=v0.2;path=truncate-input` plus `Retry-After` on reject. keeps client-side UX sane.
Anjali R: approved as an RFC follow-up. Security needs to review downgrade rules for data-flow differences and billing must sign off.
Maya Patel: I'll draft RFC + oncall playbook: quick rollback (force-route to dedicated region), manual pin model, emergency quota bump. Example Grafana alert: `fallback_rate > 5% for 1m` with labels region/model.
Lisa G: add a QA gate: when fallback engages >1% for any tenant, run small eval set to detect quality regressions and send to research.
Tomas Chen: can someone provision a guinea_test tenant to simulate abuse patterns (repeated huge prefixes + small budgets)? @Anjali R? :grimacing:
Anjali R: I can spin up a test tenant and script load tomorrow morning.
Maya Patel: thanks. I'll open the RFC and include runbook steps + metrics + example headers. ping me for review.
InfraBot: link: https://r.redwood/r/rfc/4718 (draft) :link:
Lisa G: :thumbsup:
